title: Responses translation layer: gap catalog and graceful fallback policy for OpenAI Responses parity
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Goal: produce a prescriptive, implementable translation layer that maps OpenAI Responses semantics to Redwood's Responses-compatible API while cataloging functional parity gaps and defining graceful fallback behaviors. Scope covers streaming delta semantics, function/tool call lifecycle (invoke/callback/return types), structured outputs (json_schema and enforcement), stop token handling, streaming diagnostics/events, and metadata/role drift. Outcome: a gap catalog, concrete adapter spec with example mappings, and a fallback policy so hosted customers do not experience hard errors when models or upstream semantics differ.
acceptance_criteria: A parity matrix exists mapping OpenAI Responses fields to Redwood internal types and streaming frames
Adapter implements streaming delta -> incremental token frame mapping without changing existing client SDKs
Tool/function calling flows handled with explicit lifecycle events (call_request, tool_exec, tool_result) and documented fallback when tool metadata missing
Structured-output schemas are validated server-side with a configurable enforcement level (warn/strict) and tests covering common failure modes
Canary rollout plan and monitoring thresholds defined and implemented
tasks: Audit OpenAI Responses spec and collect variant behaviors observed in our fleet
Draft parity matrix and gap catalog (fields, streaming frames, error semantics)
Design adapter wire format for streaming delta frames and function call events
Implement translator module that runs as a middleware in the runtime to normalize incoming upstream streams
Add server-side schema validator with enforcement toggle and explainable error payloads
Create end-to-end tests including simulated upstream deviations and perf regression checks
Write docs/examples and update SDK behavior notes
Run canary with 5% of traffic and monitor canary metrics for 48 hours before wider rollout
tradeoffs: Strict schema enforcement prevents bad outputs but may break existing customers — mitigation via enforcement levels and rollout
Real-time translation layer adds CPU overhead; we can optimize hot paths but initial canary will increase per-request cost
Full fidelity of OpenAI streaming deltas requires emitting more frame types; keeping client surface stable means some upstream events are summarized rather than passed through
rollout_plan: Phase 1: internal integration tests and unit coverage (2 weeks). Phase 2: deploy translator behind a feature flag, run 5% canary for 48h (metrics below). Phase 3: expand to 25% with customer opt-in for strict enforcement. Phase 4: default enable with opt-out and migration notes in SDKs.
canary_metrics: error_rate for downstream clients (5xx/4xx) attributable to translation
success rate of tool invocation flow (call->exec->return) vs baseline
customer-reported errors or regression tickets created within 72 hours
